abstract: Risk of cancer of the testis was related to nondescent and hernia in a comparison of 596 testicular cancer patients and 602 unaffected men who had been in active service in the U.S. Army between 1950 and 1970. Medical histories were obtained from routine service records. Undescended testis was associated with a testicular cancer risk 8.8 times that of normal. Among cancer patients with a history of undescended testis, seminomas were nearly twice as frequent as in the remaining patients. Of 14 patients with unilateral undescended testis, 12 had the tumor on the side of the defect. Testicular cancer risk was estimated to be 2.9 times higher in men who had reported having had an inguinal hernia than in those who had not. Side of hernia and side of tumor were not associated; histologic type was not related to history of hernia.
abstract_ja: 1950年から1970年の間に米国陸軍で勤務した精巣がん患者596例と、影響を受けていない男性602例を比較し、停留精巣と鼠径ヘルニアが精巣がんのリスクと関連するかを検討した。病歴は定期的な兵役記録から得た。停留精巣は精巣がんのリスクを正常の8.8倍と関連していた。停留精巣の既往を持つ精巣がん患者では、セミノーマが他の患者の約2倍の頻度で認められた。鼠径ヘルニアの既往がある男性は、ない男性と比べ精巣がんのリスクが2.9倍と推定された。片側の停留精巣を持つ14例のうち12例で、腫瘍は欠損側に生じていた。ヘルニアの側と腫瘍の側は関連しておらず、組織型もヘルニアの既往とは関係がなかった。
